idiom_name: Compose higher-order composables, Modifier extensions and CompositionLocal
implementation_notes: In Jetpack Compose a component is a @Composable function and behaviour is added by wrapping it in another composable that takes a composable lambda (content: @Composable () -> Unit) - a higher-order function over components, which is the pattern's mechanic with the wrapper written inline. The official documentation describes modifiers as decorating or augmenting composables, so a Modifier extension function is the shared, chainable form of the same idea, while CompositionLocal replaces prop injection for cross-cutting values. A hand-written wrapper composable is still justified when the enhancement must own composition-scoped state or must exist as a node (a provider, a boundary, a scoped theme); Kotlin's by-delegation covers the object form when a component is a class.
pitfalls: Composable functions may only be called from composition: invoking a composable lambda outside a composable scope (an ordinary callback) throws at runtime.
Modifier order is semantically significant - padding before background renders differently from background before padding - so reordering a shared modifier silently changes layout.
A wrapper composable introduces its own recomposition scope: state read inside it recomposes the wrapper and everything below unless reads are deferred into lambdas.
